names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Ερμάς, Πατρόβας, Λίνος, Γάιος και Φιλόλογος, Απόστολοι από τους Εβδομήκοντα», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 5 ноября ст. ст., «Святой Ерм, апостол от 70-ти», with the rank words and the see left off; the see is recorded as the office. The line itself gives the name in the genitive. His life pages are headed «Святой Ерм (Ерма), апостол от 70-ти», so the calendar itself gives «Ерма» as a variant of the same name; the nominative of the name page is what the folder stores.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 5. новембар ст. ст., „Св. апостоли: Патров, Ерма, Лин, Гај и Филолог.“ — «Св. апостоли» left off, of which «Св.» is not a rank and «апостоли» is the `apostle` grade `types` keeps, and the heading gives the five nothing but five bare names in the nominative, so the second of them is the whole of the form (section 6). It is one letter longer than the Russian «Ерм» this folder already stores and folds with nothing; `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured 0 other holders. «(5 November)» in the display name is this corpus’s own.

feast.note: The name page also lists «4 января (70 ап.)», the synaxis of the Seventy Apostles, which is a synaxis and not a second feast; this folder renders on 5 ноября ст. ст. only. **The 8 марта his life pages add has now been read on the day page itself and it does keep him**: «Ап. Ерма (I).» is the second entry of 8 марта ст. ст., and the «Ерма» of it links name page **792**, the same page the 5 ноября line links and the same page whose two lives this folder already cites. So the Russian keeps him on both days, and the 8 March day is recorded here rather than as a second row, one row per church being the schema. This replaces a note that said the 8 марта day page «was not read either».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 ноября ст. ст. — «Апп. от 70-ти Патрова , Ерма , Лина , Гаия , Филолога (I).»
source.note: The same calendar's line for 8 марта ст. ст. is «Ап. Ерма (I).», behind the same name page 792, whose «Дни памяти» are «4 января (70 ап.), 8 марта, 5 ноября».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.11.2025 (5. новембар ст. ст.) — „Св. апостоли: Патров, Ерма, Лин, Гај и Филолог.“

attestations.note: The second name of the day’s second entry, an ENUMERATED COMPANY OF FIVE with no «и други» at the end, so all five folders take the same one heading, whole, with its closing full stop. URL year 2025. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Св. апостоли» is the `apostle`, «Беху из седамдесет апостола» the Seventy, and `bishop` the see the body gives him; `martyr` is this folder’s own from an earlier page and this entry neither repeats nor contradicts it — it says only that all five «преселише се у царство Христово». `dates` UNTOUCHED at the first century: no year at all. **AND THE SEE THIS BOOK GIVES HIM IS NOT THE ONE IN HIS `office`.** «Ерма у Филипопољу (Рим. 14, 16)» — bishop in PHILIPPOPOLIS, where this folder’s `office` reads Bishop of Philippi in Macedonia. Philippopolis in Thrace and Philippi in Macedonia are two cities and this is a larger disagreement than Patrobas’s two towns of one bay; `office` holds one string and NOTHING WAS CHANGED. The disagreement is recorded here and in the life. The reference «(Рим. 14, 16)» is copied as printed and not corrected: the name stands at Romans 16, 14, and the two numbers read as transposed. NO `locations`, NO `related` ROW: the other four are `related` here in both directions already. NO FOLD: `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured «Ерма» at 0 other holders, and the string is one letter longer than the Russian «Ерм» this folder already stores and does not fold with it. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: The century days.pravoslavie.ru prints at the end of its line for 5 ноября ст. ст., «Апп. от 70-ти Патрова , Ерма , Лина , Гаия , Филолога (I).». The shorter of his two life pages says the same of him in words: «Святой апостол от 70 Ерм был епископом в Филиппополе, мученически скончался в I веке.» Neither doxologia.ro nor saint.gr gave this folder any year, so this is the first date it carries.
